summary: The change speeds up widget lookups with a cache, but the cache key ignores the tenant, so one tenant can read another's widgets.

skipped.reason: The run failed twice: timed out after 30 minutes

findings.title: Cached widgets are never invalidated
findings.body:
Updating a widget leaves the old copy in the cache until the process restarts, so readers see stale data.

Evict the entry in `updateWidget`.

findings.title: Typo in the cache log message
findings.body: Fixed in #5: the message is reworded there.

findings.title: The cache key ignores the tenant
findings.body:
Two tenants asking for widget 7 share one cache entry, so the second tenant receives the first tenant's data.

Include the tenant id in the key:

```suggestion
const key = `${tenantId}:${widgetId}`
```

questions: Should the cache be shared between processes?
